titleTag: Can Two People Get Earlier US Visa Appointments Together?
h1: Can Two People Get Earlier US Visa Appointments Together? How Group Bookings Behave
deck: A family booking is not two problems, it is one harder problem. You are no longer looking for an opening, you are looking for several on the same day, and the odds fall away faster than most people expect.
metaDescription: How US visa group bookings work: why a family needs adjacent slots rather than one, when to split a group, and how the costs multiply per person in 2026.

coverSpec.title: A group US visa booking moves as a unit, so a family needs several openings on one day rather than one
coverSpec.desc: Applicants grouped in a single scheduling account are moved together, so an earlier date requires enough openings on the same day for the whole group. Single cancellations, which are the main supply of earlier appointments at busy posts, rarely arrive in twos and threes. Every fee also multiplies: the application fee, the $250 visa integrity fee where it is collected, and the $750 expedite where it applies, are all charged per applicant.

faq.q: Can a family get US visa appointments on the same day?
faq.a: Yes, and in most cases that is how the system is designed to work. Applicants grouped in one scheduling account are booked and moved together, which keeps a family on the same date without you having to coordinate it. The difficulty is not getting the same day, it is getting an earlier same day at a busy post.

faq.q: Why is it harder to reschedule a family than one person?
faq.a: Because the group moves as a unit, so you need enough openings on a single date for everybody. At busy posts the main supply of earlier appointments is individual cancellations arriving one at a time, and those rarely appear in twos and threes on the same day. A family of four is looking for a much rarer event than a solo applicant is.

faq.q: Can I reschedule just one person out of a group?
faq.a: Usually not through the portal. Where applicants share a scheduling account the system moves them together and an individual change is often not offered at all. Splitting a group is a support request rather than a self-service action, and attempting to force it can still consume one of your reschedule attempts.

faq.q: Should I book my family separately to keep flexibility?
faq.a: It is a real trade-off rather than an obvious yes. Separate bookings give each applicant independent flexibility, which makes earlier dates easier to find. They also create the risk of the family ending up on different days at different times, more appointments to keep track of, and separate reschedule allowances to manage. For most families the grouped booking is the right default, and the exception is where one member has a hard deadline the others do not.

faq.q: Do children need their own appointment and their own fees?
faq.a: Yes. Each applicant needs their own DS-160 and their own application fee, and the $250 visa integrity fee where the post is collecting it applies per person as well. Nothing in this process has a family rate. A family of four looking at a B-1/B-2 application is $740 in application fees and $1,000 in integrity fees before anything else.

faq.q: How does the $750 expedite work for a family?
faq.a: Per applicant, which is what makes it hard for families. At Mission Mexico or Mission Canada, where the pilot runs, a family of four is $3,000 in expedite fees on top of $740 in application fees. It is non-refundable, so a trip that falls through takes the money with it. For a family the arithmetic on rescheduling is very different from the arithmetic for one traveller.

faq.q: Does the biometrics appointment rule apply to each person?
faq.a: Yes, where your country uses a separate biometrics or document collection appointment. Each applicant's biometrics has to sit before the interview, generally by at least a day or two, so the data is processed and available to the consular officer. When you move a group interview earlier, check every member's biometrics date, because one person out of order can cause a cancellation.

cta.heading: Families are the cases where a wide date range matters most
cta.body: That is not a sales line, it is the arithmetic on this page. Needing four openings on one day is a much rarer event than needing one, and the only thing that meaningfully improves the odds is widening the window you will accept. If you are trying to move a family booking at a busy post, tell us how many of you there are, your current date and the widest range your plans allow, and we will tell you honestly how it looks before you commit to anything.
